question: A consultant wants to paste a client's confidential strategy deck into Claude in order to build a summary. What matters most before doing so?
options: A) Whether the deck is short enough to fit into a single conversation without needing to be split.
B) Whether Claude's summary will be accurate enough to send to the client without any further editing.
C) Whether the client's contract permits their material to be processed in a third-party tool at all.
D) Whether the consultant's colleagues will be able to see the summary in a shared project workspace.
correct_answers: C) Whether the client's contract permits their material to be processed in a third-party tool at all.
explanations: Length is a practical detail and says nothing about whether the material may be used.
Output quality is a separate question from whether the input was allowed to be shared.
Correct. Contractual confidentiality terms decide whether the material may be entered anywhere in the first place.
Internal visibility matters later; permission to process the client's material comes first.
